subject: Production throughput budget & fallback plan
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: John Doe <john.doe@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production throughput budget & fallback plan

Hi John —

Thanks again for taking the demo this morning. Per our call I wanted to summarize the performance targets you mentioned and outline a pragmatic next-step plan so your engineering team can validate SLO fit. High level notes:

- Target traffic profile: steady daytime baseline ~200 rps, peak bursts ~450 rps for <10 minutes. (See attached traffic export.)
- Latency expectation: p95 <= 150ms for non-streaming requests; streaming chunk latency target <= 100ms between chunk frames for interactive UI.
- Concurrency: assumed average concurrency 6, headroom to 12 for peak spikes.
- Token budget: average response ~120 tokens; average request prompt ~80 tokens.

Action items we propose (quick MAP):
1) Lightweight perf validation run: Redwood will provide a curated load script and a dedicated short-lived test deployment (2–4x the baseline) to simulate peak bursts. Goal: measure p95 and CPU/GPU utilization across runs.
2) Fallback plan: if p95 >200ms at peak, we recommend automated fallback to a smaller quantized variant + prefix caching for historical prompts. We'll include a model-matrix and cost delta.
3) Acceptance criteria: sustained 10-minute window at 300 rps where p95 <= 200ms on the chosen config OR documented trade-offs accepted by ACME infra lead.
4) Timeline: we can provision the test window as early as next Tuesday (9/8).

I've attached the post-demo SLO checklist and your traffic export. Please confirm the test window preferences and whether your platform team needs network/VPC peering or will use hosted endpoints.

Best,
Olga
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192

Attachments: rdw-post-demo-slo-checklist.pdf, acme-traffic-patterns.csv
From: John Doe <john.doe@acmecorp.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: ACME Platform Team <platform@acmecorp.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production throughput budget & fallback plan

Thanks Olga — useful summary. A couple quick clarifications from our side before we lock in a test window:

1) The peak bursts you saw were from a scheduled campaign; sustained peaks are unlikely but can recur twice/day for up to 7 minutes.
2) For streaming UX we care most about first-byte latency on chunk start and then stability of chunk-to-chunk timing. If the first chunk takes >120ms users complain.
3) Network: we will use your hosted endpoints for the initial test (no VPC peering yet).

We can do Tuesday 9/8 in the afternoon (PST). Can you confirm expected cost for a single 2-hour test window so I can budget approval? Also loop in your solutions engineer for the run.

—John
John Doe

Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2026 13:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production throughput budget & fallback plan

Olga / Aditya —

Notes for the test run and a rough cost estimate:

- Test config proposal: 4 instances of c4-like dedicated workers (prod-sim), model: rw-large quantized (8-bit) for primary; fallback: rw-medium int8.
- Expected steady-state cost for a 2-hour run (hosted): ~$480 (compute + tokens). If we need additional headroom to reach 450 rps reliably, budget up to $1,200 for a 2-hour window. I'll confirm exact pricing after capacity check.
- Perf checks to capture: p50, p95, p99, GPU utilization, batch sizes, KV cache hit rate, and token footprint. We'll also run streaming-specific checks: first-chunk latency, inter-chunk jitter.
- Fallback automation: propose an A/B style canary where we route 100% -> primary for baseline; if p95 delta > 40ms over 2 consecutive 3-minute windows, auto-switch to fallback model and report. We'll need ACME to accept brief rollbacks during the test.

I'll prepare the load script and a short runbook (where to look for logs, how to abort). Olga — do you want me to include a prepopulated Kibana/console link in the Drive folder?

Rishi
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 3 Sep 2026 15:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production throughput budget & fallback plan

John —

Thanks — Tuesday 9/8 14:00 PST is booked on our end. Quick confirmations and next steps:

- Test window: Tue 2026-09-08 14:00–16:00 PST. We'll provision hosted test instances and send the load script an hour prior.
- Cost: estimate conservative budget $1,200 for the window (we'll only bill actual usage); ADAM (finance) approved a credit hold if we need an extra hour for reruns.
- Acceptance: we'll capture the 10-minute sustained window at 300 rps with p95 <= 200ms; streaming first-chunk p95 <= 120ms. If that is met, we mark the perf qualification step as passed and proceed to a short pilot in your staging environment.
- Fallback: Rishi will push the canary automation. We will include a short rollback playbook in the Drive folder.

Please reply if ACME wants narrower acceptance thresholds; otherwise we'll proceed as above and share the Drive links + load script on Monday.

Talk soon,
Olga
